children: Indonesia used 10.7 million kilolitres of palm oil-based biodiesel from January to early September, as it rolled out the B50 blend nationwide, an Energy Ministry presentation at a parliament hearing showed on Tuesday.

The total comprised 7.27 million kilolitres of B40 distributed in the first half and 3.42 million kilolitres of B50 supplied as of September 7, amounting to about 64% of the total allocation for the year.

Indonesia raised its 2026 biodiesel allocation to 16.75 million kilolitres to meet demand under the B50 programme, which is a 50-50 blend of palm-based fuel and conventional diesel and was launched in July to curb fuel imports and contain rising energy costs stemming from the Middle East conflict.

"B50 trials have been completed for vehicles, agricultural and mining machinery, maritime transport and power generation, demonstrating the fuel's durability," senior energy ministry official Eniya Listiani Dewi told the hearing.
Railway trials were still underway and targeted for completion in December, Eniya said.

Separately, state energy company Pertamina told the same hearing that B50 was available at 94% of its fuel stations. A three-month transition period to use up remaining B40 stocks and complete the nationwide transition to B50 will finish at the end of September.
During the hearing, Eniya also outlined plans to accelerate Indonesia's ethanol-blended gasoline programme.
A blend of 10% crop-derived bioethanol and 90% gasoline, known as E10, will be rolled out starting from 2027, rising to 20% in 2028, Eniya said.
